questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion for emphasis in a hypothetical scenario?
options: If she *had* been told the truth, she would have reacted differently.
Only if he *had* finished his work would he leave the office.
Had it not been for his support, she would have failed the exam.
Unless she *had* studied more diligently, she wouldn’t have passed.
questions.answer: Only if he *had* finished his work would he leave the office.

questions.question: Which cleft sentence correctly restates the subject-verb-object structure to highlight the object?
options: What the project *was* that caused such delays was unclear.
It *was* the unexpected budget cuts that forced the team to rethink their approach.
The decision *was* made by the committee that led to the merger.
What was surprising was that no one noticed the error until after the launch.
questions.answer: It *was* the unexpected budget cuts that forced the team to rethink their approach.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a third conditional with a nuanced subjunctive structure?
options: If she *had* known the risks, she would have taken the job.
If she *had* been given the opportunity, she would have accepted it immediately.
She would have left if she *had* been offered a better salary.
Had she *known* the truth sooner, she would have avoided the situation.
questions.answer: If she *had* been given the opportunity, she would have accepted it immediately.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly employs ellipsis with a formal register and implied meaning?
options: He said he’d be back soon, but he never arrived. (He never arrived.)
The proposal was rejected without further discussion. (The proposal was rejected.)
She was surprised by his absence; he’d mentioned he’d call. (She’d mentioned he’d call.)
The agreement was finalised after many revisions. (The agreement was finalised.)
questions.answer: The proposal was rejected without further discussion. (The proposal was rejected.)

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines complex clauses with a formal, nuanced conditional structure?
options: Although she had warned him, he still made the same mistake.
Had he not been distracted, he would have completed the task on time.
The project’s success depended on the team’s ability to adapt, which they did not.
If resources *had* been available, the project would have been completed earlier.
questions.answer: The project’s success depended on the team’s ability to adapt, which they did not.
